topic: Moser's Circle Problem: The Mystery of Dividing the Circle
target_audience: High school students interested in combinatorics and sequence patterns

sections.title: The Hook: How many pieces?
lecture_lines: Two points give two regions. [Asset: hook_animation]
animations: Place point_1 on circumference, label 'P1', color='#FFFF00'
Draw chord if points exist, count 1 region inside, color='#00FFFF'
Place point_2 on, label 'P2', draw chord P1-P2, count 2 regions, color='#00FFFF'
Show text '1 point = 1 region; 2 points = 2 regions' near the center, color='#FFFF00'

sections.title: Building the Sequence: Data Collection
lecture_lines: Pattern suggests two to power n-1. [Asset: data_animation]
animations: Display sequence 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 on screen in grid, color='#00FF00'
For n=3, add 3rd, draw all chords, highlight 4 regions, color='#FFFF00'
For n=4, add 4th, show 8 regions forming, color='#FFFF00'

sections.title: The Counter-Intuitive Reveal
lecture_lines: Geometry reveals the true count. [Asset: reveal_animation]
animations: Flash text 'n=6' in large font, color='#FF0000'
Draw, draw 6th point, connect all possible chords inside circle, color='#FFFFFF'

sections.title: The Logic: Combinatorial Geometry
lecture_lines: Formula: C(n,4) plus C(n,2) plus one. [Asset: logic_animation]
animations: Animate 4 points on, mark their unique intersection point, color='#FFFF00'
Show result 31 again using the new formula, color='#00FF00'

sections.title: Conclusion: The Power of Proof
lecture_lines: C(n,4) plus C(n,2) plus one. [Asset: conclusion_animation]
animations: Flash summary text 'Observation vs. Rigor', color='#00FFFF'
Display final verified formula: 'C(n, 4) + C(n, 2) + 1 = Regions', color='#00FF00'
Show 'Proof reveals the truth!' as final message, color='#FF00FF'
